page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for tile and integer operations.

The server is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include 236 GB of local disk storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2156.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth read-only large block benchmarks fall into the lower performance tier. Redis SET operations also register in the lower quartile, while database operations and static web serving throughput maintain average tier performance.

Given its high memory density relative to the 4 vCPUs, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring significant memory footprints without demanding massive parallel CPU scaling. The hardware profile and benchmark results make it suitable for relational database hosting, memory-intensive caching layers, text processing, and small-scale language model inference.
